title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.115-117). Sigma = Sigma_A is a lattice with least element 0_Sigma attached to an 'atelier' A. Sigma is not assumed distributive. Its elements serve as 'parts' of spatial figures.

Commensurability (p.115). A family of elements of Sigma is 'commensurable in the set-theoretic sense' if it lies in a sub-lattice Sigma' of Sigma that is a Boolean algebra. Grothendieck notes this is strictly stronger than pairwise commensurability.

Chains of figures. A chain A_0 << A_1 << ... << A_n of discrete spatial figures in Sigma is a successive refinement of finite families of pairwise disjoint nonzero elements. Such a chain is called commensurable, and from this page on 'commutable', if the union of the A_i is.

Lemma 3 (p.115-116). For each a_i in A_i, let a''_i be the 'new part' of a_i relative to A_{i-1}, as in Lemma 2. This is a relative complement of the join of the elements of A_{i-1} lying under a_i. Set A''_i = {a''_i nonzero}, A''_0 = A_0, and A = union of the A''_i. Then:
- each A''_i consists of mutually disjoint elements;
- the A''_i are mutually disjoint from one another, so A is one disjoint family;
- the chain (A_i) is commutable iff the single disjoint family A is commutable.
Grothendieck adds that he had earlier called this property 'admissible' and will now say 'commutable'.

The reduction. Commutability of a whole refinement chain is thus reduced to commutability of one disjoint family: a 'triangulation' of the chain into its new pieces.

Axiom Atmorph 3. This axiom subsumes Atmorph 1 and 2: for every diagram of figures F_0 << ... << F_n in the atelier, the corresponding chain A_0 << ... << A_n in Figspatdisc(Sigma) is commutable. The purpose is to guarantee that whatever the morphisms of figures produce lives, locally, inside a Boolean world, where set-like reasoning is legitimate.

The NB. It proposes a category Figelspatcomm(Sigma) of commutable elementary spatial figures. The axioms Fig 2, 3 would be imposed with a stronger order relation.

Outcome (p.117). Grothendieck finds that this stronger order is probably not transitive. Commensurability of {g, g'} and of {g v g', f'} need not imply commensurability of {g, g', f'}. He concludes the approach 'ne semble pas marcher', except when Sigma itself is Boolean, i.e. distributive.
errors: Lemma 3 tacitly needs relative complements a''_i to exist and be well defined. In a non-distributive lattice, relative complements need not exist and need not be unique. So the definition of A''_i and the equivalence 'chain commutable iff A commutable' need a hypothesis such as sectional complementation or orthomodularity that is not stated on this page.

Not an error on this page itself: the programme it launches (a category of commutable figures with a stronger order) is judged non-viable by Grothendieck on the next page, because transitivity fails in non-distributive Sigma.

ideas.what: Family of lattice elements is 'commensurable/commutable' iff contained in a Boolean sub-algebra; strictly stronger than pairwise commutability
ideas.modern_name: compatible / commuting elements generating a Boolean block (quantum logic, orthomodular lattices); Foulis-Holland type theorems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff-von Neumann (1936); Foulis, Holland (1960s); Kalmbach (Orthomodular Lattices, 1983)

ideas.what: Lemma 3: reduce commutability of a refinement chain to that of the disjoint family of 'new pieces'
ideas.modern_name: common disjoint refinement / atoms of the Boolean algebra generated by a chain of partitions

ideas.what: Axiom Atmorph 3: every chain of figures in an atelier yields a commutable chain of spatial figures
ideas.modern_name: local Booleanness / 'classical contexts' axiom for a geometry over a non-distributive lattice of parts

missed.claim: Grothendieck's notion of 'commutable' families in a non-distributive lattice of parts is essentially the quantum-logic notion of compatibility. In both, families generate a Boolean sub-algebra, and pairwise compatibility is not enough in general. His transitivity obstruction (p.117) is exactly what orthomodularity cures, via Foulis-Holland-type results. Even the name 'commutable' matches the quantum-logic usage of 'commuting'. No link between his 1986 'ateliers' and orthomodular lattices or topos-theoretic quantum logic (Boolean contexts) seems to be recorded.
missed.quote: pour que le diagramme (A_i) soit commutable i.e. ∪A_i commutable, il faut et il suffit que A le soit (i.e. qu'il soit "admissible", mais je préfère dorénavant le terme "commutable")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: His failing axiom system might be repaired by assuming Sigma orthomodular. That would place the 'ateliers' alongside the Butterfield-Isham / Döring-Heunen 'Boolean contexts' approach. This is of historical interest, but the attempt was abandoned by him.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an exploratory foundational page in an abandoned approach (rejected on the next page). The lattice-theoretic content is elementary. The only interesting point is an unremarked parallel with quantum-logic compatibility.
transcription_corrections: 'il {+suffit+} et il suffit' should read 'il faut et il suffit'.
'forment d'éléments mutt[?] disj.' reads as 'sont formés d'éléments mutuellement disjoints'.
'Atmorph[?] 3' is best read 'Atmorph 3', the third axiom on morphisms of the atelier, said to subsume the two previous ones.
The last line 'la imagine[?] obtenant' is probably 'la catégorie obtenue en [prenant]', continuing on p.117 with 'l'axiome Fig 2 et 3'.
'(ou une notation pareille Σ)' is a marginal insertion, roughly '(ou une notation pareille pour Σ)'.
